transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Hi. Thanks. Well, what finally made me come in is that I just keep making these small, but really embarrassing mistakes. Like, I'll turn in applications or research notes, and I'll find out later that I mislabeled an artwork date or completely skipped a question. And the thing is... I honestly thought I had checked them over before submitting them. It's just getting pretty frustrating.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on a task, even when you want to pay attention?

I don't think so, no. When I sit down to work on something, I feel like I'm paying attention. I don't really notice myself zoning out or losing focus when I'm trying to get a task done. It's more just... making those small mistakes I mentioned, even though I feel like I'm focused on it the whole time.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking your work over and over, even after you already know you’ve looked at it?

No, not really. I usually just look it over once, maybe twice, and think it's fine. I don't sit there checking it over and over again. I just... I assume I caught everything when I looked at it the first time, so I submit it and move on. It's only later that I realize I missed something.
Do you often feel worried or on edge, even when there isn’t one specific problem causing it?

No, not really. I mean, I get frustrated when I realize I messed up on an application or something, but I don't just feel worried out of nowhere. I'm usually pretty relaxed unless there's an actual reason to be stressed out.
Do you often start tasks but have trouble finishing them?

No, not really. If I sit down and start something, I usually finish it. I mean, I might make those careless mistakes along the way, like I mentioned, but getting to the end isn't really the issue. I don't usually leave things half-done. Once I start a task, I just push through until I submit it.
Are you easily distracted by things going on around you while you're working?

Yeah, definitely. If I'm sitting at my desk trying to read or write, almost anything can pull my focus. Like, if a siren goes by outside, or I hear someone talking out in the hallway... I just lose my place. Even just a random thought, like an idea for an exhibit or something, will pop into my head, and I'll get completely sidetracked. Sometimes twenty minutes will go by before I even realize I stopped working.
Looking back, were you already this easily distracted as a child?

Yeah, I think so. Even back in elementary school, my teachers would write notes saying that I had good ideas, but I'd always forget to turn in my worksheets or I'd somehow lose the instructions. I was always missing little details like that. Honestly, nothing really got turned in unless my parents checked my backpack every single night to make sure I had everything.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive presentation: the patient reports frequent careless mistakes, marked distractibility by external stimuli and internal thoughts, and a childhood history of similar inattentive symptoms requiring parental monitoring. Symptoms appear persistent from childhood and are causing current academic/work-related impairment. There is no evidence here for generalized anxiety or compulsive checking as primary explanations.
